evidence_inputs: The landing is correct on its own terms: current.book is a single vmapped program, bit-identical to the superseded scan on the tiled CPU fixture at 7c9d86bd..f13542848 and agreeing to floating-point reassociation (3.6e-12 worst, 4.5e-16 relative) on the H200 certificate carrier.

The product change is 3 lines and costs nothing in scope; the whole node turns on it. Two done-when clauses are not delivered and are registered follow-ons: the 10,000-cell rung (pending the carrier-requalify node's device store) and the one-Picard-image state wall (the flux-map image lives on the operator's own sample block while current.book consumes flux at the topology read's per-cell stencil, so no Picard-state number is quotable without an operator-side partition reconstruction owned outside this fence).

The batched program's peak device memory is 7.7-23.7 GB against the scan's 0.71-3.03 GB, a 7.4-10.6x increase, and it compiles 1.1-1.7x slower; the fragment flags this as the binding constraint on scaling to 10,000 cells.

The base/head arm delta is zero (6 failing ids both arms, all test_analytic_certificate_moments, from a missing NOVA_BOOK_RESULTS fixture), so no regression is introduced, but the base arm's log provenance is unverified (see finding; the log names tree=/tmp/vb-base while its recorded nova.__file__ resolves to the head worktree).

findings.text: the identity test compares the production book against _reference_book (the preserved sequential scan) and reddens on the declared booking mutation, but no assertion fails if book is reverted to the sequential scan itself: reinstating the base jax.lax.scan(cell, None, ...) at nova/equilibrium/current.py:272 leaves every assertion green, so done_when(1) 'no Python loop or sequential scan over cells remains on the path' has no guard and a future un-vectorisation would pass the suite.

the base arm header asserts tree=/tmp/vb-base (and manifest baseline_suite revision 7c9d86bd), but the same header's own provenance line prints nova.__file__=/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/nova-a0f1e0938fc2/s21-nova/vectorize-booking/nova/__init__.py[?]; the module under test resolved to the head worktree, not the base scratch tree, so the recorded baseline revision is not what the log shows imported. The six failures are a KeyError 'NOVA_BOOK_RESULTS' reached before booking and are identical in both arms, so the zero delta stands; the defect is in the provenance of the base arm, not in the conclusion.

done_when(2) and (3) name identity and per-step walls 'at about 2,000, 5,000 and 10,000 cells' and 'on analytic states and on one-Picard-image states'; the 10,000-cell rung and every one-Picard-image wall are withheld (plan-verdict partial, blockers in the manifest). Both are externally blocked -- the 10,000-cell machine on the carrier-requalify node's device store and the Picard image on an operator-side reconstruction outside this fence -- so neither is repairable within this node, but the delivered measure is a proper subset of the one the done_when states.
